decisive_kills.reason: The proposed core bridge is private user documents plus a public structured complaint schema. Current generic AI/document tools can already draft collection documents from user facts, while the official complaint form itself enumerates required fields and attachments. No distinct operator-controlled data or execution rail is required for the basic output.

The official complaint rail is free and public. The governing regulation encourages public-interest legal services for SME payment disputes. Search found paid collection/legal services, but not evidence that SMEs currently pay for the narrow self-serve complaint-packet compiler as a standalone product.

Low-complexity factual drafting/completeness work is increasingly free or generic-AI substitutable; high-complexity disputed cases require legal judgment, negotiation, preservation, litigation/arbitration or representation and are already served by licensed lawyers and collection engagements.

The official platform owns the submission and result rail. User-provided documents alone do not create a reusable proprietary edge, and outcome feedback is not naturally returned to a third-party compiler.

evidence.fact: Current lawyer guidance frames enterprise receivables as a full-lifecycle legal service including negotiation, letters, mediation, litigation, arbitration, preservation and enforcement.

evidence.fact: A current paid collection engagement shows outcome-based lawyer bids at 6%, 9% and 10% of recovered funds, evidencing paid demand for the high-complexity professional layer rather than the narrow document compiler.

evidence.fact: Free generic AI document generation already covers collection letters and related legal-document drafts, supporting commodity pressure on simple drafting.
